summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every Hindi video gets 100-1400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 30 views. The best video was the PIR motion sensor one, which got far more views, likes, shares and saves than anything else. Videos on 'how does this thing around me know?' get the most attention, while generic or sound-based titles (smoke alarm, ultrasonic, remote) get little engagement. Sample size is small and videos are only days old, so treat this as early signal.
winningPattern: Everyday sensor that seems to 'magically' react to you (motion, street light, phone orientation), explained in Hindi. Hook is a surprising claim or a curiosity question in Hinglish ('X aapko dekhta nahi!' / 'Kaise pata chalta hai?'), with a 🤔 emoji and #shorts. Instagram Reels is the main traction platform; YouTube Shorts is weak so far, though the PIR video and the English Arduino video got the most YouTube views.
doMore: Pick relatable daily-life sensors people see every day (lifts, ATM, automatic lights, fan remote) and open with a twist claim like 'Yeh aapko dekhta nahi!'
Use a bold 'myth-bust' first line before the question, since the PIR title with that format beat the plain-question titles
Prioritise Instagram Reels for posting and testing; add a clear 'save this for your project' call to action to raise saves and shares
Make follow-up videos on the PIR winner (PIR + Arduino build, why it fails in heat) to reuse the proven topic
Test one or two YouTube titles in a different style (shorter, with the English keyword like 'PIR Sensor') to find out why YouTube is lagging
stopDoing: Plain 'X kaise sense karta hai?' titles on niche items like smoke detectors, which get low shares and saves
Posting several near-duplicate topics in a row (two smoke alarm videos in 3 days) that split the audience
